issues.description: The problem statement and the template define/expect an instance method named attend(course:) on Developer (taking a Course? parameter). In the solution repository the extension on Developer implements a method named participateIn(course:) instead of attend(course:). Additionally, the solution's Client.swift calls myself.attend(course:), but Developer.swift in the solution does not provide attend(course:), causing an internal inconsistency in the solution (it would not compile) and a mismatch with the problem/template. This discrepancy will confuse students about the correct method name and prevents the solution from matching the specified API.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution match the problem/template API by renaming the Developer extension method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (with the same Course? parameter and behavior). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use participateIn(course:) consistently — but prefer changing the solution to attend(course:) so it aligns with the specified exercise and with the template and Client invocation. Ensure the method name and signature are identical across problem statement, template, Client, and solution so students are not confused and the code compiles.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an instance method named attend(course:) on Developer (problem statement: "Implement an instance method `attend(course:)`"; template: an empty stub `func attend(course: Course?) { }`). The solution repository, however, implements this method under a different name (`func participateIn(course: Course?)`) which creates a direct naming mismatch. This breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the described requirement and the implementation, and also causes inconsistency between the solution's Developer implementation and the solution's Client usage (Client calls `attend(course:)` while Developer defines `participateIn(course:)`). Students will be confused about which method name to implement and may be unable to find or call the correct method in the provided codebase.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the method in the solution to match the problem and template by changing `func participateIn(course: Course?)` to `func attend(course: Course?)`. Also ensure all call sites (e.g., Client.swift) use the same name. Alternatively, if `participateIn` is preferred, update the problem statement and template to use `participateIn(course:)` consistently — but the simplest fix is to align the solution to the existing problem/template name `attend(course:)`.
